checklist.evidence: Treat values like `0000:00:00 00:00:00` and blank strings as missing.
Sort by sub-second value first, then by original name. Add `_01`, `_02`, and so on.
The tool only previews unless `--apply` is passed.
If a file's name already matches its target, mark it as a no-op. This makes it safe to run the tool twice.
Write `.exifrename-log-<timestamp>.jsonl` *before* each step and flush it each time.
picks which date tag to trust, parses it, handles sub-seconds and time zones
`IMG_1.HEIC`, `IMG_1.xmp`, `IMG_1.AAE`, and `IMG_1.MOV` (when it's a Live Photo pair) all get the same new name stem.
Characters like `:` and `?` aren't allowed in Windows file names, so the default template uses `-` and `_`.

traps.evidence: No silent overwrites: Use `os.rename` with an existence check rather than `os.replace`.
